claim_judgments.rationale: Claim C0000 accurately conveys the mandatory duty under 29 CFR 825.303(a) that an employee must give notice to the employer as soon as practicable when the timing of unforeseeable FMLA leave is not known in advance.
Claim C0001 captures the advisory standard in 29 CFR 825.303(a) stating that it generally should be practicable to provide notice within the employer's usual and customary notice timeframes.
Claim C0002 preserves the permission and conditions under which a spokesperson may give notice on the employee's behalf if the employee is unable to do so personally.
Claim C0003 reflects the regulatory example/exception where an employee caring for a child receiving emergency treatment for severe asthma is not required to leave the child to report the absence.
Claim C0004 reflects the contrasting illustration where the child requires only home treatment and rest, establishing the expectation of prompt notice after inhaler use.
Claim C0005 correctly articulates the general requirement in 29 CFR 825.303(b) that an employee must provide sufficient information for an employer to determine whether the FMLA may apply.
Claim C0006 correctly enumerates the non-exhaustive categories of information that may satisfy the notice requirement depending on the circumstances.
Claim C0007 correctly states the negative requirement/exemption that a first-time leave seeker need not expressly reference or assert rights under the FMLA.
Claim C0008 accurately captures the obligation for subsequent leave requests to specifically reference either the qualifying reason or the need for FMLA leave.
Claim C0009 conveys the rule that merely calling in sick without providing further details is insufficient to trigger employer obligations.
Claim C0010 captures the employer expectation regarding informal inquiry to obtain additional required information.
Claim C0011 correctly states the employee's duty to respond to employer questions designed to determine FMLA eligibility.
Claim C0012 correctly conveys the consequence that failure to answer reasonable inquiries may lead to denial of FMLA protections.
Claim C0013 properly captures the core requirement of 29 CFR 825.303(c) to comply with employer notice policies absent unusual circumstances.
Claim C0014 correctly captures the example of employer policy options (calling a specific number or individual).
Claim C0015 correctly represents the emergency medical treatment exception to call-in procedures until stabilization and phone access.
Claim C0016 accurately states the potential relief from written advance notice requirements in emergency FMLA-qualifying situations.
Claim C0017 correctly reflects the sanction that leave may be delayed or denied if an employee fails to follow usual procedures without unusual circumstances.
